I will keep things simple and steady this year. I am in Quzhou County on the North China Plain, so the cropping pattern I trust most is winter wheat followed by summer maize. At my age, I will not spread myself across too many crops. Wheat and maize are the crops I know best, the market is clear, the machines are easy to arrange, and the risk is lower than trying something fancy. I will put all my land into this rotation so I can manage it in one rhythm.

For wheat, I will use improved seed, not old saved seed, because I want even emergence and better disease resistance without making management too complicated. I will give enough base fertilizer and then a topdressing of nitrogen when the wheat starts to stand up strongly. Water is important here, so I will irrigate a few key times instead of watering too often. I will spray only when needed for weeds, aphids, rust, or scab risk, because I do not want to waste money. I will use rotary tillage for convenience and because it matches how I want the field prepared.

After wheat harvest, I will plant summer maize right away. I will choose a hybrid maize because maize responds well to better seed and gives me more stable yield. I will keep fertilizer moderate, with enough nitrogen and some phosphorus and potassium, and I will focus on one good watering at the critical stage if rain is short. I will keep pesticide applications limited and only handle the common problems like armyworm, corn borer, and weeds. This is the plan I would follow because it fits my age, my experience, my local climate, and the need to keep labor and risk under control.
